text:
The Blues' week was about family and the trade market. Keith Tkachuk dropped the puck with his sons Matthew and Brady, now both Panthers, on the night St. Louis honored him. And Jordan Binnington's name keeps coming up in rumors, with Edmonton the team people connect him to, though Elliotte Friedman wasn't sold on it yet.

The reason the Binnington talk has room is Joel Hofer. He's on a heater, .932 with 5.4 goals saved above expected over his last five starts, including a 1-0 shootout win over Utah. St. Louis is 9-9-2 with 20 points, and the process is middling: 49% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances). The goalies have been good, allowing almost six fewer goals than expected. The shooters have given almost eight back.

That cold finishing has a face. Pavel Buchnevich has one point in his last ten games on chances that usually produce five. Robert Thomas, Dylan Holloway and Jimmy Snuggerud play the most minutes together and break even, and Snuggerud has become a waiver-wire name for good reason. Mason McTavish's line with Connor McMichael and Jonatan Berggren pushes the pace. Logan Mailloux is back from injured reserve, with Adam Jiricek sent down.

Our playoff odds sit at 29%. What we'd watch: whether Buchnevich and the shooters warm up before management decides what kind of season this is, and whether a Binnington move clears the crease for Hofer.
